procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Orissa at Cuttack
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 20.01.2023 of the High Court of Orissa at Cuttack in BLAPL No.6803 of 2022, rejecting the appellant's second bail application.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellant filed a bail application (BLAPL No. 6803/2022) in the High Court of Orissa. This was the second bail application, the first having been rejected on 07.07.2022. The High Court rejected the second bail application on 20.01.2023, citing the fact that a co-accused who had been released on bail had not surrendered.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court against the High Court's order rejecting his bail application. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's order, and directed the High Court to reconsider BLAPL No. 6803/2022, taking into account that charges have been framed and 19 prosecution witnesses are proposed to be examined. The Supreme Court requested the High Court to dispose of the application at the earliest, preferably within two months.

directions: The impugned order is set aside.
The High Court will take up BLAPL No. 6803/2022 and pass orders on the same.

issue.issue_text: Whether the High Court was justified in rejecting the appellant's bail application solely on the ground that a co-accused, who had been released on bail, had not surrendered.

facts: The appellant, charged under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, had been in custody for two years and 11 months.
The High Court rejected the appellant's application for bail.
The Supreme Court identified that the sole reason for the High Court's rejection was that a co-accused, who had been released on bail, had not surrendered.
law: The Supreme Court established the legal principle that the failure of a co-accused to surrender after being released on bail is not a 'germane factor' to consider when deciding the bail application of another accused person.
application: The Court analyzed the High Court's order and found that it had improperly denied bail to the appellant based on a factor that was not relevant to the appellant's own case.
The Court reasoned that an accused person's eligibility for bail should be assessed on its own merits, and the actions of a co-accused are not a valid ground for denial.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the High Court was not justified in rejecting the bail application on the sole ground of the co-accused's failure to surrender. Consequently, the Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's order, and sent the matter back to the High Court for reconsideration on its merits.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the High Court was justified in rejecting the appellant's bail application solely on the ground that a co-accused, who had been released on bail, had not surrendered.
appellant_arguments: The fact that a co-accused, who was released on bail, has not surrendered is not a germane or valid reason to deny bail to the appellant.
The appellant has been in custody for a significant period of two years and 11 months.
The appellant's father has undergone surgery, which is a compassionate ground for consideration.
respondent_arguments: The appellant had previously made another unsuccessful attempt to secure bail from the High Court, indicating no change in circumstances.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The fact that a co-accused who was released on bail has not surrendered cannot be a germane factor to decline bail to another co-accused.
obiter: The fact that charges have been framed and that a number of prosecution witnesses are proposed to be examined are relevant factors for consideration in a bail application.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found that the High Court's sole reason for rejecting the appellant's bail application was the fact that a co-accused, who had been released on bail, had not surrendered. The Supreme Court held that this is not a germane or relevant factor to consider when deciding whether to grant or deny bail to the appellant.
legal_tests_applied: Whether a factor used to deny bail is 'germane' to the specific accused's application.
policy_considerations: An accused's application for bail should be decided based on factors relevant to that individual, not on the unrelated actions of a co-accused.
